hypotheses.statement: At least some DEE42B-associated CACNA1A variants have been functionally characterized and show altered CaV2.1 channel behavior consistent with pathogenicity in epilepsy/encephalopathy.
hypotheses.rationale: Recent translational work on CACNA1A missense variants in neurodevelopmental disorders and the broader channelopathy literature suggest functional assays are available for disease variants. system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You gather evidence that tells hypotheses apart. Each was tested on its own; now they are weighed against each other.

## Read the local results with care

- Scores and support/refute counts come from experiments that can themselves be flawed: a bug, a bad measurement, a narrow check.
- Look at the artifacts and the evidence behind each result before trusting it.
- Where two hypotheses predict different things, find out which happened. Compare their metrics part by part: a claim that loses overall can win somewhere.

## What to submit

- New observations, each with its observation region and the retrieval ids it rests on.
- For each observation, a verdict (supports, refutes, neutral) on every hypothesis it bears on, with one line why.
- Record what you checked, not what you expect. Call submit_evidence once.

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You gather evidence that tells hypotheses apart. Each was tested on its own; now they are weighed against each other.

## Read the local results with care

- Scores and support/refute counts come from experiments that can themselves be flawed: a bug, a bad measurement, a narrow check.
- Look at the artifacts and the evidence behind each result before trusting it.
- Where two hypotheses predict different things, find out which happened. Compare their metrics part by part: a claim that loses overall can win somewhere.

## What to submit

- New observations, each with its observation region and the retrieval ids it rests on.
- For each observation, a verdict (supports, refutes, neutral) on every hypothesis it bears on, with one line why.
- Record what you checked, not what you expect. Call submit_evidence once.

messages.content:
**Task**

Find the published literature on this rare disease.

Disease: DEVELOPMENTAL AND EPILEPTIC ENCEPHALOPATHY 42B
Symbol: DEE42B
Phenotype MIM number: 621692
Gene: CACNA1A

Find every paper that reports patients with this disease or establishes its genetic cause: the original report(s), later case reports and cohorts, and functional studies of the disease variants. Papers may describe the disease under an older or different name, or only by gene and phenotype. Use PubMed; do not consult OMIM.

**Observation regions**

3 of 10 regions (room for more)
- axis `literature source`  [3 regions, 52 observations]
  - `PubMed case series and reports`: Single-case or family reports, often with phenotype described under epilepsy, developmental delay, ataxia, or channelopathy terms rather than DEE42B.  [17 observations]
  - `PubMed cohort/genetics studies`: Exome/genome or epilepsy cohorts reporting CACNA1A as a disease gene and tallying affected individuals.  [16 observations]
  - `PubMed functional studies`: Electrophysiology, cell-based, iPSC, animal-model, or in vitro experiments on disease variants.  [19 observations]

**Hypotheses**

- [h1] DEE42B is supported first by de novo or segregating CACNA1A variants reported in early-onset epilepsy/neurodevelopmental case reports and broad exome studies, even when the papers do not use the DEE42B label.  (tested, region `Human-case genetic diagnosis`)
  - rationale: The search surfaced the original de novo epileptic-encephalopathy paper and later CACNA1A epilepsy/genotype-phenotype papers, suggesting the disease literature is distributed across phenotype-first reports. This would be falsified if CACNA1A never appears in patient reports with epilepsy/encephalopathy phenotypes.
  - evidence: 10 supporting, 0 refuting
  - local test notes: I checked PubMed literature for CACNA1A / DEE42B across case reports, cohorts, and functional studies. The evidence remains consistent with the hypothesis: patient literature exists under phenotype-first terms (epilepsy, developmental delay, neurodevelopmental disorder, ataxia) and includes de novo or segregating CACNA1A variants in early-onset epilepsy/encephalopathy cohorts, plus functional studies on disease variants. I did not find evidence contradicting the claim; no revision was warranted. No artifact was built in this iteration.
- [h2] A substantial portion of the disease literature consists of later cohorts that expand the phenotype from epilepsy alone to mixed CACNA1A-related neurodevelopmental disease, helping define seizure types, developmental severity, and treatment response.  (tested, region `Cohort expansion`)
  - rationale: The 18-patient CACNA1A-associated epilepsy cohort and the 47-person CACNA1A-related disease series indicate aggregation studies rather than isolated cases; these papers may be the main source of patient counts and clinical spectrum. This would be falsified if all relevant papers were singleton case reports with no cohort-level synthesis.
  - evidence: 11 supporting, 0 refuting
  - local test notes: Checked PubMed for cohort/series, case reports, and functional studies around CACNA1A/DEE42B. The retrieved literature continues to show multiple aggregation studies plus at least one singleton case report and at least one functional paper, so the hypothesis is supported rather than contradicted. No revision was needed.
- [h5] At least one published DEE42B/CACNA1A variant has been functionally shown to alter CaV2.1 channel gating or neuronal excitability in a direction that supports pathogenicity for early-onset epilepsy/encephalopathy.  (tested, region `Variant-specific functional validation`)
  - rationale: The current literature already contains functional studies of CACNA1A disease variants, but the next step is to test whether any of the specific DEE42B-linked variants have direct electrophysiologic validation. This is falsified if all functional papers are on unrelated CACNA1A phenotypes or only discuss clinical interpretation without variant-level assays.
  - evidence: 4 supporting, 0 refuting
  - local test notes: I found direct variant-level functional validation for CACNA1A neurodevelopmental/epilepsy-associated missense variants in 2025, plus multiple clinical cohort and case-report papers linking CACNA1A to early-onset epilepsy/encephalopathy. I did not need to revise the claim because the evidence supports it rather than contradicting it.
- [h6] DEE42B is most often reported as part of a broader CACNA1A neurodevelopmental spectrum, with papers describing epilepsy plus developmental delay, ataxia, migraine, or mixed neurologic features rather than isolated epileptic encephalopathy.  (tested, region `DEE42B overlaps broader CACNA1A neurodevelopmental spectrum`)
  - rationale: The cohort and case literature already suggests mixed phenotypes and expanding syndrome definitions. This hypothesis is falsified if the DEE42B-associated papers are restricted to pure epilepsy/DEE without additional CACNA1A phenotypic overlap.
  - evidence: 8 supporting, 0 refuting
  - local test notes: Collected PubMed evidence that CACNA1A disease papers repeatedly frame the condition as a broader neurodevelopmental/channelopathy spectrum, with epilepsy plus ataxia, developmental delay, migraine, hemiplegia, stroke, or mixed neurologic features. Key supporting papers: Lipman 2022 (47 individuals; expanded to developmental delay, epilepsy, paroxysmal dystonia, neuropsychiatric disorders), Le Roux 2021 (18 patients with CACNA1A-associated epilepsy; abstract cites EA2/SCA6/FHM spectrum), Gudenkauf 2020 (child with early stroke and intractable epilepsy; abstract explicitly notes hemiplegic migr
- [h8] The published DEE42B/CACNA1A literature includes strong evidence for loss-of-function or haploinsufficiency mechanisms, but PubMed-abstract-verified evidence for gain-of-function CACNA1A variants specifically linked to DEE42B remains unconfirmed in the retrieved literature.  (tested, region `Variant class determines functional direction`)
  - rationale: Supported LOF evidence is clear from PMID 39460936 and related functional work (observations o18, o39, o44), plus DEE42B-relevant clinical reports and cohorts (o31, o32, o35, o37, o38, o43). However, the retrieved literature did not yield an abstract-confirmed DEE42B-specific gain-of-function CACNA1A paper; negative observations o34, o41, and o45 explicitly note this gap. Because the original claim that both LOF and GOF are already established is too strong, it should be narrowed rather than kept as-is.
  - refines h7
  - evidence: 3 supporting, 0 refuting
  - local test notes: Checked PubMed case reports, cohorts, and functional hits for CACNA1A/DEE42B. Found direct DEE42B/EIEE42 patient literature plus a functional haploinsufficiency paper, but no abstract-confirmed DEE42B-specific gain-of-function paper in the retrieved set.

**Observations so far**

- [o1] There are multiple cohort/series papers on CACNA1A-related epilepsy/neurodevelopmental disease. PMID 34102571 reports 18 patients with CACNA1A-associated epilepsy and treatment response. PMID 35722745 reports 47 individuals with CACNA1A-related disease and explicitly says the spectrum has expanded to developmental delay and epilepsy. PMID 40111503 is a multicenter study of phenotypic variability in CACNA1A mutation cases with epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders. PMID 23934111 is a large epileptic encephalopathy exome cohort and includes CACNA1A among de novo candidate genes. PMID 41370402 is a functional/clinical study of CACNA1A missense variants found in neurodevelopmental disorders, indicating later aggregation studies beyond singleton cases.  [region `PubMed cohort/genetics studies`, sources 35722745, 34102571, 40111503, 23934111, 41370402]
  - supports h2: These papers show that a substantial part of the literature is cohort-level, not just isolated case reports, and they expand from epilepsy-only cohorts to mixed neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
- [o2] The literature is not limited to singletons: the 2021 18-patient epilepsy series and the 2022 47-person CACNA1A-related disease series are the main patient-aggregation reports surfaced in this search. They combine seizure phenotyping with developmental/neuropsychiatric features, suggesting the disease literature includes repeated clinical synthesis rather than only isolated case reports.  [region `PubMed case series and reports`, sources 34102571, 35722745, 40111503]
  - supports h2: This aligns with the hypothesis that later cohorts broaden the phenotype and define seizure types, developmental severity, and treatment response.
- [o3] Functional work exists on disease variants. PMID 41370402 characterizes functional and clinical impacts of CACNA1A missense variants from neurodevelopmental disorder cases, and PMID 39460936 reports CACNA1A haploinsufficiency effects in neurons/iPSC-derived systems with reduced synaptic function and increased intrinsic excitability.  [region `PubMed functional studies`, sources 41370402, 39460936]

[region `PubMed case series and reports`, sources 34102571, 35722745, 40111503]

[region `PubMed functional studies`, sources 35722745, 40111503]

[region `PubMed case series and reports`, sources pubmed:case_reports_1, pubmed:case_reports_2]

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each) or a `revive` of an eligible shelved hypothesis.
- Call submit_exploration once.

You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each) or a `revive` of an eligible shelved hypothesis.
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each) or a `revive` of an eligible shelved hypothesis.
- Call submit_exploration once.

h_regions.description: Hypotheses about whether DEE42B-causing CACNA1A variants act through gain-of-function, loss-of-function, or haploinsufficiency, and whether different variant classes map to distinct electrophysiologic signatures.

h_regions.name: DEE42B overlaps broader CACNA1A neurodevelopmental spectrum
h_regions.description: Hypotheses that DEE42B papers will be embedded within broader CACNA1A phenotypes such as epilepsy, developmental delay, ataxia, hemiplegic migraine, or mixed neurodevelopmental disorder, rather than presenting as a narrow syndrome only.

h_regions.name: Variant-specific functional validation
h_regions.description: Primary papers that test one or a few DEE42B-associated CACNA1A variants in cells, neurons, organoids, or animal models to connect genotype with channel behavior and excitability.

h_regions.name: Allele-specific mechanism splits
h_regions.description: Different CACNA1A variant classes or even individual alleles can map to distinct functional directions or model-system effects, such as loss-of-function, haploinsufficiency, altered gating, or excitability changes.

h_regions.name: From case reports to functional follow-up
h_regions.description: The literature path begins with phenotype-first case reports and then branches into cohort aggregation and variant-level functional validation for the same CACNA1A alleles.

h_regions.name: DEE42B nested in mixed CACNA1A phenotypes
h_regions.description: DEE42B papers are expected to sit inside a wider CACNA1A spectrum that includes epilepsy, developmental delay, ataxia, migraine, stroke, and other neurologic signs.

o_regions.name: PubMed case series and reports
o_regions.description: Single-case or family reports, often with phenotype described under epilepsy, developmental delay, ataxia, or channelopathy terms rather than DEE42B.

o_regions.name: PubMed cohort/genetics studies
o_regions.description: Exome/genome or epilepsy cohorts reporting CACNA1A as a disease gene and tallying affected individuals.

o_regions.name: PubMed functional studies
o_regions.description: Electrophysiology, cell-based, iPSC, animal-model, or in vitro experiments on disease variants.

o_regions.name: Allele-specific PubMed trails
o_regions.description: Search PubMed using exact amino-acid substitutions, cDNA changes, or report-named variants from the patient papers to find matching functional studies, family reports, and follow-up citations.

o_regions.name: Phenotype-first patient reports
o_regions.description: PubMed case reports and single-family papers that name epilepsy, DEE, developmental delay, ataxia, stroke, or migraine rather than the DEE42B label.
